lessons.title: Value vs Reference Types
lessons.body:
Structs and enums are value types; classes are reference types. Value types are copied on assignment.

```swift
struct Point { var x: Int }
var a = Point(x: 1)
var b = a
b.x = 2 // a.x is still 1
```

quickCheck.explanation: Structs are value types; classes are reference types.

questions.prompt: What is the default access level in Swift?
questions.explanation: Declarations are `internal` by default — visible within the module.
Arrays are value types, so `b` is an independent copy; `a` stays [1, 2].

codeSnippet.code:
var a = [1, 2]
var b = a
b.append(3)
print(a)

questions.prompt: Tell me about a time you disagreed with a teammate on a technical decision.
questions.explanation: Use STAR: Situation, Task, Action, Result. Focus on the resolution and what you learned.
questions.rubric: Strong answers name the disagreement concretely, show respect for the other view, describe how a decision was reached (data, prototype, escalation), and end with an outcome plus a lesson.
